headline: Light snow showers taper off today, followed by a frigid Friday night with lows in the single digits and teens, then a weaker storm brings more wind and Sierra snow Saturday evening through Sunday before a break Monday and Tuesday ahead of possible Thanksgiving-week storms.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A Winter Storm Warning runs until 10 AM for the Tahoe area and the northeastern California Sierra as a final round of snow showers adds 2–5 inches along the Sierra crest, up to 2 inches at Truckee and Lake Tahoe and up to 6 inches on higher peaks, falling at up to a half inch to an inch an hour. South of US-50, including the Mammoth area, isolated light snow showers linger into the afternoon before tapering off by evening, and there is a 5% chance of thunder along the Sierra crest this afternoon. Around Reno, bands of light snow up to an inch could slow the morning commute along US-395 between Hallelujah Junction and Stead and on I-580/US-395 near Carson City; Reno and Sparks will most likely miss out, but a small shift in either band (about a 20% chance) could bring light snow there through about 10 AM. Tonight turns dry and especially frigid, with lows in the single digits and teens, cold spots such as Bodie, Bridgeport, Truckee and the Carson Valley possibly dipping below zero, roads icing as daytime melt refreezes, and freezing fog possible in northeastern California and Sierra valleys, especially near Truckee.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday stays dry and chilly until the next storm arrives, offering a possible Sierra travel window if roads improve. This weekend's storm comes in two waves with increasing winds: the first brings rain and snow showers Saturday afternoon and evening, mainly from Tahoe northward, and the second, stronger and more widespread round arrives Sunday afternoon and evening. It is much weaker than the last storm, but there is a 40%+ chance of 6 inches of snow on passes such as Donner and Carson, while Sierra communities below 7,000 feet see lighter amounts (a 20–50% chance of 2 inches at lake level). Cold air keeps snow levels down to the valley floors, and Reno and other western Nevada towns have a 10–30% chance of a trace to an inch by Monday, when the storm departs.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Another break between storms is expected Monday and Tuesday, which may be the best travel window ahead of Thanksgiving. More storms are possible around the holiday, with a 40–60% chance the active, stormy pattern continues through Thanksgiving week. Confidence that far out is low, so holiday travelers should keep checking the latest forecast.

watch_for: Icy roads overnight as melted snow refreezes, and freezing fog near Truckee and other Sierra valleys Friday night into Saturday.
Sunday afternoon and evening snow on Sierra passes such as Donner and Carson (40%+ chance of 6 inches).
Additional storms around Thanksgiving; Monday and Tuesday look like the best travel window.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in this morning's Sierra snow and the dry, very cold break, less certain exactly where the Reno-area snow bands set up, moderately confident in the weekend storm's mountain snow, and have low confidence in storms around Thanksgiving.
